attacker_capabilities: competent adversary with access to physical device and capabilities to induce specific conditions
insider threat with knowledge of device operation

countermeasures.description: Utilize radiation-hardened flip-flops for key storage to protect against SEU-induced bit flips.
countermeasures.residual_risk: Low, as radiation-hardened techniques are well-established but may increase area and power consumption.
countermeasures.title: Radiation-Hardened Key Storage

countermeasures.description: Design circuits with balanced PMOS/NMOS transistor usage and use dynamic voltage scaling to minimize prolonged high voltage bias conditions.
countermeasures.residual_risk: Medium, due to potential performance trade-offs.
countermeasures.title: NBTI-Aware Circuit Design

countermeasures.description: Integrate performance monitoring sensors to detect degradation from HCI and trigger alerts for maintenance.
countermeasures.residual_risk: Medium, as detection relies on accurate threshold settings and may produce false positives.
countermeasures.title: Performance Monitoring Sensors

countermeasures.description: Incorporate error-correcting code (ECC) for data paths and key storage to correct transient errors from SEUs.
countermeasures.residual_risk: Low for transient errors, though increased latency and area may occur.
countermeasures.title: Fault-Tolerant Design with ECC

countermeasures.description: Perform regular stress tests to analyze and compensate for performance degradation caused by NBTI and HCI under controlled conditions.
countermeasures.residual_risk: Medium to Low, depending on consistency and thoroughness of testing schedules and analysis.
countermeasures.title: Regular Stress Testing and Analysis

critic_findings.evidence: No documented analysis of software or firmware-based threats affecting key handling and encryption operations.
critic_findings.finding: The analysis lacks a comprehensive threat model addressing all possible attack vectors.
critic_findings.recommended_fix: Expand threat scenarios to include software and cross-domain attacks (e.g., firmware tampering, side-channel attacks).

critic_findings.evidence: Both "NBTI-Induced Timing Leak" and the general "NBTI" description highlight similar effects without differentiation.
critic_findings.finding: Duplicated failure descriptions for NBTI under different titles and threat scenarios.
critic_findings.recommended_fix: Consolidate NBTI-related mechanisms into a single, comprehensive explanation with specific attack paths.

critic_findings.evidence: Countermeasures mention low or medium residual risks without quantifying impact or likelihood, making prioritization difficult.
critic_findings.finding: The risk levels and residual risks of countermeasures are not consistently quantified.
critic_findings.recommended_fix: Develop a risk matrix or scoring system to evaluate and justify the residual risk levels stated for each countermeasure.

critic_findings.evidence: The component description lacks assumptions that could affect the effectiveness of mitigation strategies.
critic_findings.finding: Assumptions regarding operational conditions are missing, such as expected environmental ranges and adversary knowledge limits.
critic_findings.recommended_fix: Explicitly list environmental and operational assumptions, such as maximum radiation exposure levels and adversary capabilities, that underpin threat analysis robustness.

critic_findings.evidence: Countermeasures like dynamic voltage scaling and performance monitoring lack details on implementation and expected performance impacts.
critic_findings.finding: Countermeasure descriptions are vague regarding implementation specifics and trade-offs.
critic_findings.recommended_fix: Provide detailed implementation guidelines and performance benchmarks for each countermeasure, outlining expected trade-offs and limitations.

critic_findings.evidence: Lack of documentation linking performance reduction to a potential increase in successful timing attacks impacting confidentiality.
critic_findings.finding: Title for 'HCI-Induced Performance Degradation Attack' suggests a focus on integrity rather than performance degradation links to confidentiality impacts.
critic_findings.recommended_fix: Clarify the linkage between performance degradation and potential security impacts, focusing on how this might facilitate or hinder other types of attacks.

deployment_assumptions: Multi-agent analysis includes device physics, adversarial threats, lifecycle risks, and manufacturing considerations

failure_mechanisms.mechanism: Movement of metal atoms due to high current density, leading to open or short circuits.
failure_mechanisms.name: Electromigration
failure_mechanisms.security_relevance: Potential for unexpected failures possibly leading to data corruption.

failure_mechanisms.mechanism: Degradation of transistors due to prolonged bias voltage at high temperatures.
failure_mechanisms.name: Bias Temperature Instability (BTI)
failure_mechanisms.security_relevance: Slow degradation might lead to performance issues or expose timing side channels.

failure_mechanisms.mechanism: Charge carriers gain high kinetic energy and get trapped in the gate oxide, affecting transistor behavior.
failure_mechanisms.name: Hot Carrier Injection (HCI)
failure_mechanisms.security_relevance: May degrade performance, affecting ability to perform timely encryption.

failure_mechanisms.mechanism: State alteration of flip-flops due to cosmic ray or alpha particle strikes.
failure_mechanisms.name: Single Event Upset (SEU)
failure_mechanisms.security_relevance: Could cause incorrect encryption results or leak sensitive data if key bits are affected.

failure_mechanisms.mechanism: Insulating layer failure under high electric fields, leading to short circuits.
failure_mechanisms.name: Gate Oxide Breakdown
failure_mechanisms.security_relevance: Possible catastrophic failure affecting encryption operations.

failure_mechanisms.mechanism: Specific to PMOS transistors, increased threshold voltage over time due to prolonged negative gate voltage.
failure_mechanisms.name: NBTI (Negative Bias Temperature Instability)
failure_mechanisms.security_relevance: Could reveal timing vulnerabilities or degrade encryption performance.
trigger_conditions: Prolonged negative bias at high temperatures

failure_mechanisms.mechanism: Expansion and contraction due to temperature changes, leading to mechanical fatigue.
failure_mechanisms.name: Thermal Cycling
failure_mechanisms.security_relevance: Potential for hardware faults leading to unintended device behavior.

failure_mechanisms.mechanism: Sudden discharge of static electricity damaging components.
failure_mechanisms.name: Electrostatic Discharge (ESD)
failure_mechanisms.security_relevance: May cause latent failures compromising device reliability.

scope.component_boundaries: The boundaries of the AES engine include the encryption and decryption logic, key expansion module, input/output data buffers, and control interface.
scope.component_definition: The AES engine is a hardware component designed to perform Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) encryption and decryption operations efficiently.
normal_operating_conditions: Operates within specified voltage and temperature ranges
Receives clock signals synchronized with the SoC
Input data and keys are provided by secure software modules

security_requirements.requirement: The AES engine shall use radiation-hardened flip-flops for key storage to protect against Single Event Upsets (SEUs) that could cause bit flips.
security_requirements.title: Radiation-Hardened Key Storage
security_requirements.verification_method: Hardware simulation and testing under radiation exposure

security_requirements.requirement: The AES engine shall be designed with balanced PMOS/NMOS transistor usage and include dynamic voltage scaling to mitigate Negative Bias Temperature Instability (NBTI).
security_requirements.title: NBTI-Aware Circuit Design
security_requirements.verification_method: Circuit simulations demonstrating balanced PMOS/NMOS use and voltage scaling effectiveness under high temperature bias conditions

security_requirements.requirement: The AES engine shall integrate performance monitoring sensors to detect degradation from Hot Carrier Injection (HCI) and trigger maintenance alerts.
security_requirements.title: Performance Monitoring Sensors
security_requirements.verification_method: Functional testing with calibrated sensors under controlled HCI conditions

security_requirements.requirement: The AES engine shall incorporate error-correcting code (ECC) for data paths and key storage to correct transient errors from SEUs.
security_requirements.title: Fault-Tolerant Design with ECC
security_requirements.verification_method: Simulation and physical testing of ECC implementation under SEU scenarios

security_requirements.requirement: The AES engine and associated systems shall undergo regular stress testing to identify and mitigate degradation from NBTI and HCI effects.
security_requirements.title: Regular Stress Testing and Analysis
security_requirements.verification_method: Regularly scheduled stress tests analyzed for performance degradation patterns

summary: The AES engine is a hardware component designed to perform Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) encryption and decryption operations efficiently.
